name: Operational budgeting and forecasting
one_line: The forward-looking money plan of an organisational unit and the running comparison of that plan against what actually happened: budget submissions and consolidations, forecasts and reforecasts, variance commentary, headcount and capex models, and the sign-off trail around them. The anchor is a PLANNING ROUND for a unit and a period — money that has not happened yet, or money being explained after the fact — which is what separates it from a custodial accounting record held with an institution. Absorbs the legacy row ops.operating-plan-budget. A PLACEHOLDER TEMPLATE ROW written to J-DEPTH: it recognises the situation and writes NO field rows, because the business_operations schema declares none.

proposed_fields.example: FY2026, Q3 FY26, the 2026-27 planning round
proposed_fields.why_no_existing_key: SECONDING, NOT MINTING. This key is proposed by the landed business_operations SCHEMA row and this entry adds no variant, no synonym and no second spelling - it exists only to record that of the four rows in the family that cycle annually, this is the one that needs the key most, and to put a THIRD-PARTY CONFLICT in front of R1c that the schema row could not see. The conflict: the landed finance.small-business-bookkeeping row raises the identical concept in its own open_question under a DIFFERENT NAME - it asks whether "the shared vocabulary gain a destination-eligible reporting_period key", having rejected tax_year for the same reason the schema row rejects it. One concept, two spellings, proposed independently by two families that contest the same workbook, is exactly the bug D6 exists to prevent. R1c must adjudicate fiscal_period and reporting_period as ONE question, not two, and whichever spelling survives must be the one both families use. The underlying argument is the schema row's and is not restated here.
proposed_fields.destination_eligible_why: As proposed on the schema row, unchanged: it is a period, not a person, so 00's authorship-as-destination prohibition does not reach it. Not first - “For document and record domains, project, function, or subject usually comes before time because putting year first scatters related work across calendar folders.”
proposed_fields.reliability_why: As proposed on the schema row, unchanged: a fiscal-period token pattern co-occurring with a period-context term in the same labelled block. This row writes no regex and no term list. Without that rule the honest ceiling drops to `possible`.

deterministic: PRECONDITION: every entry below is a DETECTION signal and never an extraction licence. The business_operations schema declares no field rows (D1 as narrowed, _CONTRACT rules 10 and 15, CONNECTION PR-6), so nothing here writes a domain fact; detection exists so the material is recognised, kept where this row's sensitivity says, and offered honestly. “Privacy policy must be enforced before content reaches any model or external connector.”

a management-financial table structure: a labelled period column series (months, quarters, or a plan year) crossed with a budget / forecast / actual / variance column set, over a line-item row set, WITHOUT a bank statement's account-number-and-balance header and without a double-entry debit/credit pair. The absence of the institution-and-account header is as discriminating as the presence of the variance column. “Tables matter because resumes, forms, applications, invoices, and administrative documents often place their most useful information in cells rather than body paragraphs.”

a version-and-scenario structure: several sheets or files of the same model differing only by a scenario label (base, upside, downside) or a round label (v1, v3, submitted, approved), which is a version_family shape carrying planning vocabulary.

a budget-round structure: a circulated submission template with a labelled unit or cost-centre slot, a labelled period slot, an instruction block naming a submission deadline, and an approval or sign-off line. The template travels out blank and comes back filled — both states exist in a real corpus.
a variance-commentary structure: prose paragraphs keyed to line items or cost centres, each explaining a difference between two labelled columns, usually with a favourable/adverse marker.
a driver-model structure: an assumptions block (rates, volumes, headcount, inflation) feeding a calculated schedule, with input cells visibly separated from formula cells.
an email whose labelled subject slot names a planning round or a period and whose attachment-name slot names a budget, a forecast, a submission or a model, addressed to budget holders.

parent-folder context naming a planning round, a fiscal period, or a cost centre, treated as a clue that raises plausibility once one of the structures above is present. Folder context never fires alone.
needs_llm: PRECONDITION: this world is commercially confidential and often confidential to a THIRD party, so any model step runs after P7 and under the user's policy. “Protected material should not be included in cloud-model prompts by default, should not display raw content in general group summaries, and should not be moved automatically without a user policy that explicitly permits it.”

the central determination for this row: separating a MANAGEMENT plan from a CUSTODIAL or STATUTORY record. A cash-flow forecast, a set of management accounts and a filed set of statutory accounts share vocabulary, format and often one workbook. This is NJ-J-IND-3 in its sharpest form and it is not settled here.

separating an organisation's budget from a HOUSEHOLD's or an INDIVIDUAL's. A personal annual budget spreadsheet has the same column structure; the discriminator is whether the row set is cost centres and headcount or rent, groceries and utilities — and a freelancer's is genuinely both.

separating a real submission from a blank template, a textbook exercise, a downloaded model, or a course case study. The structure is identical with values removed. “Topic answers what a file is about, while purpose answers what the file was for.”
unlabelled planning prose: an investment case, a cost-reduction memo, or a board finance narrative with no table at all.

a purpose-coherent planning packet whose members are individually unremarkable — an instruction email, a blank template, three unit submissions, a consolidation and a commentary. “The documents are content-incoherent but purpose-coherent.”
in every case above, abstention is the required outcome where the evidence does not settle it. “A model that cannot cite sufficient evidence must return unknown.”
never_alone: a spreadsheet of numbers alone. Every family on this roster produces those, and a grid of money is the tempting false file for this row — a bank export, a personal budget, a course exercise and an invoice log all match the shape.

budget vocabulary alone — budget, forecast, actual, variance, plan, run rate. Finance training material, a saved industry benchmark report and an MBA deck are dense in it and none is an organisation's plan.
a fiscal-year-shaped token alone (FY26, 2026-27). It is the single most tempting signal in this row and it appears equally on statutory returns, academic years, contract terms and sports seasons.
a currency symbol or a totals row alone.

a company, charity, or regulator gazetteer hit alone. 00 states the ambiguity for a university — “A university name alone should not create a group because Columbia can appear as an authoring school, course provider, target institution, employer, research venue, or merely a cited organization.” — and a company name is worse, appearing as employer, customer, supplier, competitor, regulator, and as the letterhead of a document that is merely ABOUT the holder. Stated as inference; 00 writes that sentence about a university, not a company.

source_type or extension alone. “treat the file extension as a routing signal rather than an assumption about meaning”, and file_kind_plausible is constitutionally never-alone (CONNECTION section 5, invariant 2).
membership in a download session that emptied a document-management system or a mail thread's attachments at once. “A session should never be treated as proof of topic”

a PDF author, producer, or company metadata string alone. “PDF metadata should be treated as supporting evidence, not as truth” — a corporate template stamps the same entity on every blank form it ever generated.
a bare 4-digit number read as a fiscal year, an entity number, a contract number, or a document version.

a filename version or finality token alone - v7, FINAL, FINAL2, (2), Copy of, ~$ - as proof that two files are one model's version family. This row is where those tokens are densest and where they lie most often, and 00 settles it: “A content-hash match supports deduplication review; a filename match alone does not.” The version_family fact is a UNIVERSAL file fact (00 lists “duplicate family, version family, and sensitivity status” among the shared set), so it is neither this row's to write nor this row's to earn activation from.

work_types: completed unit or cost-centre budget submission
grouping_reasons: one planning round for one unit: the instruction, the blank template, the submission, the challenge correspondence and the approved version — purpose-coherent even where the members share no content. “The documents are content-incoherent but purpose-coherent.”

one model across its versions and scenarios, joined by the universal version_family fact rather than by any business fact. This is the row where version_family does the most work and where filenames lie most often (v7 FINAL (2)).
one fiscal period end to end: the budget, the reforecasts, the actuals comparison and the commentary.

one unit or cost centre over several rounds — the reason most likely to tempt a unit label onto a sparse member, which is exactly what must not happen. “The graph does not automatically copy those missing facts onto sparse files.”
no group at all is a valid outcome: a single downloaded forecast template is an ordinary standalone file.
and the stop rules apply as written — “when members carry irreconcilable course, institution, project, term, or purpose facts” — two entities' budgets in one folder do not merge.

template.why: Empty by binding contract: a dimension may only branch on a field the same entry's schema declares, and business_operations declares none (D1 as narrowed, _CONTRACT rules 10 and 15, CONNECTION PR-6). That is a contract fact, not a claim that this situation has no shape — it plainly does, and it is recorded here as PROSE for whoever answers the schema row's open_question. The recommendation, held as prose: the organisational unit or cost centre that owns the plan, then the planning round or fiscal period, then the document function (submission / consolidation / forecast / commentary). The period is genuinely wanted here and is the one level a finance user reliably asks for, but it still should not be first —  Not time-first — “For document and record domains, project, function, or subject usually comes before time because putting year first scatters related work across calendar folders.” And whatever eventually lands stays a recommendation: “The system recommends an order based on the domain template, but the user can reverse, remove, add, or flatten dimensions.”

collides_with.signal: AUTHORED AGAINST A LANDED ROW AND STATED PLAINLY: the landed finance safety schema already carries “budget sheet” in its own work_types list, so finance has claimed budget-shaped bytes on the roster before this row existed. This row does not contradict that and does not ask for it to be removed. The reading it proposes instead: finance's “budget sheet” is a work_type VALUE, and 00 is explicit that work-type values are not nodes - what finance owns through it is a budget sheet that arrives with finance's own evidence, which is an institution-and-account header, a statutory issuer, or a personal holder. The discriminating evidence for this row is the absence of all three plus the presence of a unit-and-round structure: cost centres, budget holders, a submission deadline, an approval line. Where neither is evidenced, finance is a SAFETY schema and CONNECTION section 4 step 5's protective ordering means it wins the file rather than this row: “Correct abstention is a successful outcome because the product’s goal is reliable organization, not maximum file movement.” Reciprocal owed by R1c; finance carries no edge back to business_operations. Provenance: inference.

The load-bearing collision on this row and the edge form of NJ-J-IND-3. Both hold an entity's money in tables and both routinely live in one workbook. The discriminating evidence: a budget / forecast / variance column set over cost centres, with no institution and no account, supports this row; an institution-and-account header, a double-entry ledger structure, a reconciliation, or an accountant's compilation note supports bookkeeping — which sits on the finance SAFETY schema, so where they co-activate the protective ordering runs first. Where the evidence does not settle it, neither activates: “Correct abstention is a successful outcome because the product’s goal is reliable organization, not maximum file movement.” Provenance: inference.

A personal or household budget spreadsheet is structurally identical to a unit budget. The discriminating evidence is the row set and the surrounding furniture: cost centres, budget holders and approval lines support this row; rent, groceries and a single named holder support the personal row. For a sole trader the two are genuinely one file, and abstention is the correct outcome. Provenance: inference.

An investment case, an operating plan and a strategy document all carry money over a period. The discriminating evidence: a periodic plan-versus-actual comparison with variance supports this row; a goals, initiatives and horizons structure with no line-item comparison supports the strategy row. Provenance: inference.

A board finance appendix is both a pack paper and a forecast. The discriminating evidence: a pack index, attendance and resolutions support governance; a standalone model or commentary with a period column set supports this row. A pack containing both is a real file, not a defect. Provenance: inference.

A people-cost model and a compensation planning sheet are the same grid with one column different. The discriminating evidence: named individuals, salary bands, or personal review outcomes support the hr row and must be protected before any model path; roles, FTE counts and aggregate cost support this row. A single spreadsheet frequently crosses that line at one column, and when it does the stricter side wins. Provenance: inference.

A project budget and a project cost report belong to both situations. The discriminating evidence: a project identifier with milestones, a schedule, and a status structure supports project delivery; a unit-and-period planning round with a submission and approval trail supports this row. Provenance: inference.

also_holds_with.signal: One workbook holding a forecast sheet AND a reconciled-actuals sheet sourced from an accounting system is genuinely BOTH, on DISJOINT evidence: the forecast sheet's period-and-variance structure is this row's, the reconciliation's book-versus-bank balance and its accounting-package provenance are that row's. CONNECTION invariant 1 licenses carrying both edges to one neighbour precisely because the collides_with entry above names discriminating evidence, and the landed finance.research.md uses the same both-edges pattern for photos and for legal. The firewall: one evidence item - the money figure, the period label, the entity name - must never count for both sides. Provenance: inference.

falls_through_to.why: The commonest honest outcome here, because the management-versus-custodial fork is frequently unresolved on the file's own evidence. “Review Later may hold files whose meaning is partly understood but whose final location requires a future decision.”

Where a model carries named individuals, salaries, or an unannounced transaction, the protective home is the correct one. “Protected Records may represent sensitive isolated material such as passport scans, medical documents, account statements, visas, legal forms, or credentials; it should normally remain local-only and must not cause filenames or content to be exposed in model prompts.”

The home for a standalone planning artifact with no round around it — a single capex request, an approval note. “Independent Records may live under Personal/Independent Records and hold standalone certificates, notices, confirmations, forms, and PDFs that have a durable purpose but no broader group.”

Blank templates, downloaded model workbooks and saved benchmark tables are the tempting false files of this row. “Reference Clips may live under Personal/Reference Clips and hold saved visual inspiration, product references, quotes, recipes, short article captures, code snippets, or other material that is useful for later retrieval but does not belong to a current project.”

Password-protected planning packs and proprietary planning-system exports are ordinary here. “Unsupported or Encrypted may hold—or, more safely, represent without moving—password-protected archives, unreadable documents, damaged files, and unknown formats.”

sensitivity_why: A budget is usually impersonal and occasionally not, and the transition happens at one column. 00's corpus sentence names what is at stake — the corpus “can include identity documents, account statements, tax records, medical information, legal records, credentials, private correspondence, GPS metadata, employment materials, and educational records” — and a people-cost model is employment material, a cash-flow forecast attached to a bank facility is an account statement's neighbour, and a redundancy scenario names individuals. Second, and as inference: an unannounced plan is confidential to an employer whose material a person may be keeping on a personal machine, so the exposed party is often not the user. The cautious setting is the honest one. This row assigns only the catalogue value potentially_sensitive; the handling class is P7's and is not set here.
open_question: Four. (1) NJ-J-IND-3, which this row cannot settle and most needs: where does an ORGANISATION's money live? The roster's reading — statutory and custodial to the finance safety schema, forward-looking management to business_operations — is defensible but was drawn by the roster pass rather than by 00, and this row is the one that breaks if it is wrong. (2) `fiscal_period` as a canonical key (raised in the schema row's proposed_fields): this row wants it more than any other in the family, and reusing `tax_year` would quietly assert that an entity's management calendar coincides with a jurisdiction's statutory one, which it routinely does not. (3) NJ-BF-1, IS A BUDGET AND A FORECAST ONE SITUATION OR TWO? A budget is agreed once and fixed; a forecast is revised repeatedly. This row holds them as ONE situation and treats the revision sequence as the UNIVERSAL version_family fact rather than as a domain distinction - 00 lists “duplicate family, version family, and sensitivity status” among the shared file facts, and a file may be “a member of a version family” without any schema activating. The alternative, splitting the row, would mint a node whose only discriminator is a universal fact the product already computes, which is the 574's mistake in a new costume; the cost of NOT splitting is that a fixed approved budget and a fourth reforecast sit in one situation despite having different authority. (4) NJ-BF-2, ONE CONCEPT UNDER TWO NAMES: this row's proposed_fields seconds the schema row's `fiscal_period`, but the landed finance.small-business-bookkeeping row raises the same concept as `reporting_period` in its open_question. R1c must settle it once, for both families.
